Yael: Yael soulful. Yael beautiful. Very well read and city bred.
Yaiwa: Yaiwa was one of those students who never handed in a single assignment on time, and when she finally did they always seemed to be off-topic. But, they were presented with such colour and tangential brilliance that no one had the heart to expel her. Suffice to say Yaiwa received her Arts Degree, via a few years off, and neither Yaiwa nor her lecturers have any idea what she’ll do with it. Moral to the story here is those parts underlined. Amen.
Yalda: You say her name and you want to scream out, then you stop, and you listen. ‘Yalda,’ you say again. ‘Yes,’ she says, and you have nothing more to add because you know the truth. Yalda is here – here she is – and she is lovely.
Yarrow: Like a suave and delicious piece of 17th Century furniture made of priceless mahogany, Yarrow is sensitive and sensual. Here is another girl for whom most doors will just inexplicably open any time she wants. And her ego won't be doing the driving, bless.
Yasmin: Yasmin wears buckets of perfume and glossy red lipstick, sometimes a black head-band, and she has large eyes that look startled most of the time – as if she is a newly born gazelle just learning how to walk.
Yasmine: Yasmine has time and she has style. She reads other peoples’ body language as if holding an expensive vase with a pair of fine white gloves, and she hardly ever flashes her knickers.
Yazmine: Yazmine has travelled lots but Columbia is this girl's favourite country. She loves the perceived danger, she loves their musical nature, she's useless at Spanish but loves the sound of it, and yes, she loves those dark Columbian men!
Yessenia: Regrets? Zero. As a staunch optimist, Yessenia jumps into whatever she's up to with immoderation. "What's the point of doing anything in a half-arsed fashion?" she'll tell you, and she's right. I watched her get on a horse, once, that she was told might be beyond her. She mounted, the horse bolted and even after the horse dissappeared around the corner with the rider still present we could hear Yessenia screaming and laughing at the same time. (Until, of course, we heard a brief silence, then a thud, then wailing. We rushed to the scene to find Yessenia sitting on the ground sobbing with the horse ambivalently munching on green grass next to her.)
Yindi: Panic-stricken? Well, sometimes. The thing about Yindi is that, while good fortune usually follows her, she often forgets that when things don’t go her way it’s just the gods assisting her to see some kind of delicious, comedic truth. People simply adore her - men especially - because they think she needs their help. Wrong, gentlemen. As it happens, you probably need hers. And she possesses a wonderful laugh. Yindi.
Ynys: Lucky her parents didn't spell her name, Kbkd, eh? Anyway, Ynys possesses a staunch work ethic. Hold your chin up; walk straight; be proud of who you are; don't be too impulsive or wasteful - these are the some of the things that we will write on her gravestone. Thank you Ynys.
Yogi:
The fellow (or lady) who discovers Yogi as their perfect love/lover/partner will need to possess many qualities:
They’ll need to be industrious, just in order to find her.
They’ll need to like to dance and socialise.
They’ll need to be good in bed and they’ll need to be funny. And it probably helps if they’re at least a little artistic, and possibly even a little autistic, and one might help the other. 

What they don’t really need to be is particularly punctual, affluent or disingenuous. 

You got all that?
Yoko:
A backbone made of titanium means this girl is her own woman. She doesn’t suffer fools or from peer group pressure, and always always always is she looking for the best in a situation. We can only marvel at how fantastic the world would be if everyone knew themselves as well as this one, and what would be collectively achieved. 
Thanks Yoko.
Yolanda: Yolanda is often a strange, beautiful and quite ethereal woman. Years at university probably isn’t her thing, although she’d actually make a wonderful surgeon. The only downside, if you’d call it that, is that she doesn’t possess a great deal of common sense, no matter what she does. And that’s okay.
Yolande: The Acrobat. She looks great in tights, seems to have no fear and is happiest when she's off the ground - be it in plane, on a trapeze, dangerous love affair, etc etc.
Yolandi: Famous within her circle of friends, and sometimes a fair way outside it, Yolandi drives men berserk whether she’s into them or not. Yes, she attracts a lot of attention because of her general level of sensuality and the volume of her laughter, but she’s also pretty good at accidentally knocking over wine glasses and champagne bottles. The upshot of all this is that the local bar staff sigh with a haggard sense of delightful resignation whenever she walks into the joint - they know everyone is going to have fun but they also know there’s going to be a mess to clean up afterwards. Yolandi.
Yona:
Uncompromising. Yona looks you dead in the eye no matter what the scenario and in the back of her mind there are only three questions being answered:
1. Are you friend or foe?
2. Could I kill you if I had to?
3. If so what could I use nearby as a weapon?
Believe it or not, having said all that Yona is rollicking fun, she has a great laugh and she loves just as fiercely as Maria. No question.
Yoni: Hopeless with money, Yoni makes up for it with a charming, girly wit and a ravishing smile. While that alone won't appease the banks and credit companies who are chasing her, they'll be hard-pressed to find her anyway. Yoni loves to travel, no matter who is paying, and she plans to be buried on the Greek island where her grandparents were born.
Yulia: Yep, like Lizzie before her, she's quite bonkers but so what? True, she's a little clumsy and she accidentally cuts herself quite often, but she laughs hard from deep inside her belly and her little hissy-fits are funny rather than serious or problematic. She's not a bus driver.
Yunna: Ain't no moth-eaten jackets in her wardrobe, let me tell you. If she ever found one she'd insist she pay for the entire apartment building to be fumigated, immediately. (She lives in a Parisian flat and so that little exercise would not be cheap.) She'd tell you it was worth it because no way is she setting foot outside looking anything less than stunning.
Yve: If only we could make a movie of what Yve gets up to on the weekend. At 6pm every Friday, two sexy little horns appear on her head, making her all the more delicious and remarkable than she already is.
Yvette: The weary news journalist. For the past few months she's worn a flak jacket every day and can often be seen on the 7 o'clock news where she submits regular reports from Baghdad. She recently quit cigarette smoking and she's not very happy about it.
